sections.title: Section A · Textbook-style questions
sections.note: Like the "Figure it Out" questions in NCERT Ganita Prakash.

questions.text: Which of these are always even for every whole number $n$: (a) $4n+2$ (b) $n^2+n$ (c) $3n+1$ (d) $(n+1)(n+2)$ (e) $5n$?
questions.answer: (a), (b) and (d). (a) $=2(2n+1)$. (b) $=n(n+1)$ and (d) are products of two consecutive numbers. (c) and (e) are odd for some $n$.

questions.text: Put $+$ or $-$ signs between $11, 12, 13, 14$ in all possible ways. Show that you never get an odd answer.
questions.answer: With all $+$: $50$, even. Each change from $+x$ to $-x$ subtracts $2x$, which is even. So every answer is even. For example, $11-12+13-14=-2$.

questions.text: Find the remainder when $1{,}234{,}567$ is divided by (a) $2$ (b) $4$ (c) $8$ (d) $9$.
Without dividing, check whether $3{,}87{,}234$ is divisible by $2$, $3$, $4$, $6$, $8$, $9$ and $11$.
questions.answer: Even: yes. Digit sum $27$: divisible by $3$ and $9$, so by $6$. Last two digits $34$: not by $4$, so not by $8$. Alternating sum $(4+2+8)-(3+7+3)=1$: not by $11$.

questions.text: Find all the digits $x$ for which $43x2$ is divisible by $3$, and the digit for which it is divisible by $9$.
Find the digit $x$ so that $9{,}x82$ is divisible by $11$.
questions.answer: Odd places from the right: $2+x$. Even places: $8+9=17$. $(2+x)-17=x-15$ must be $0$ or $-11$, so $x=4$. Check: $9482=11\times862$.

questions.text: Write the general form of a three-digit number with digits $a, b, c$. Write the general form of the number with the digits in reverse order.
Find the digital root of $8{,}74{,}352$. What is the remainder when this number is divided by $9$?
A hall has $38$ chairs. They are arranged in rows of $6$. How many full rows are there, and how many chairs are left over? Write $38$ in the form $6k+r$.
questions.answer: $38=6\times6+2$: $6$ full rows and $2$ chairs left over.

items.v: How many rows? How many left?

questions.text: Draw a Venn diagram for the multiples of $4$, $8$ and $32$. Is there a number that is a multiple of $32$ but not of $4$?
questions.answer: No. Every multiple of $32$ is a multiple of $8$, and every multiple of $8$ is a multiple of $4$: the circles sit one inside the other.

answerPicture.caption: Every multiple of 32 is a multiple of 8, and every multiple of 8 is a multiple of 4.

sections.title: Section B · Reference-book style (as in RS Aggarwal)
sections.note: General form of numbers, reversal and missing digits.

questions.text: The sum of a two-digit number and the number with its digits reversed is $143$. If the units digit is $5$ more than the tens digit, find the number.
The difference of a two-digit number and its reversal is $54$. Find the difference of its digits. Give two such numbers.
If $21y5$ is a multiple of $9$, where $y$ is a digit, find $y$.
questions.answer: Digit sum $8+y$ must be $9$ or $18$: $y=1$ (since $y=10$ is not a digit). Check: $2115=9\times235$.

questions.text: If $31z5$ is a multiple of $3$, where $z$ is a digit, find all possible values of $z$.
questions.answer: Digit sum $9+z$ must be a multiple of $3$: $z=0, 3, 6, 9$.

questions.text: A three-digit number has digits $a, b, c$ (in that order). Show that the number minus its reversal is divisible by $99$. What is the quotient?
Find the values of the letters: $\begin{array}{r}3A\\+\,25\\\hline B2\end{array}$
Prove that the product of any three consecutive numbers is divisible by $6$.
questions.answer: Among three consecutive numbers, at least one is even and exactly one is a multiple of $3$. $2$ and $3$ have no common factor, so the product is a multiple of $6$.

questions.text: Show that $n^3-n$ is divisible by $6$ for every whole number $n$.
questions.answer: $n^3-n=(n-1)n(n+1)$: a product of three consecutive numbers, so it is divisible by $6$.

questions.text: Find the smallest number that leaves remainders $1, 2, 3$ and $4$ when divided by $2, 3, 4$ and $5$.
questions.answer: One more than the number is a multiple of $2, 3, 4, 5$: the LCM is $60$. The number is $59$.

questions.text: $N$ leaves remainder $5$ on division by $8$. Find the remainder when $3N+7$ is divided by $8$.
questions.answer: $3\times5+7=22=8\times2+6$. Remainder $6$.

questions.text: Is it possible to write $100$ as the sum of $11$ odd numbers? Explain.
questions.answer: No. The sum of an odd number of odd numbers is odd, but $100$ is even.

questions.text: Without calculating, is $2^{10}+3^{10}$ even or odd? Is $2^{10}\times3^{10}$ a multiple of $4$?
questions.answer: $2^{10}$ is even and $3^{10}$ is odd: the sum is odd. $2^{10}\times3^{10}$ contains $2^{10}$, so it is a multiple of $4$.

sections.title: Section D · Case studies
sections.note: Read the situation and answer each part.

questions.text: Case study: A school has $1{,}236$ students for a sports day.
questions.answer: (a) $1236$ is even and its digit sum $12$ is a multiple of $3$, so yes ($206$ teams). (b) Last two digits $36$: yes, $309$ groups of $4$. (c) Last three digits $236=8\times29+4$: no, $4$ students are left. (d) $1236=9\times137+3$: $3$ left over; adding $6$ makes $1242$, a multiple of $9$.
parts: (a) Can the students be divided exactly into teams of $6$?
(c) Into groups of $8$? If not, how many students are left?
(d) How many students are left when they make lines of $9$? How many more students are needed to make full lines?

questions.text: Case study: A calendar shows dates in a month. Ravi chooses a $3\times3$ square of dates.
questions.answer: (a) The dates are $n-8, n-7, n-6, n-1, n, n+1, n+6, n+7, n+8$: sum $9n$. (b) $9n$ is always a multiple of $9$. (c) $9n=153$ gives $n=17$. (d) $216\div9=24$ is the middle, so the smallest is $24-8=16$.
parts: (a) If the middle date is $n$, write all nine dates and their sum.
(b) Explain why the sum is always a multiple of $9$.
(c) The sum is $153$. Find the middle date.
(d) The sum is $216$. Find the smallest date in the square.

sections.title: Section E · Assertion and reason
sections.note: Decide whether each statement is true, and whether the reason explains the assertion.

questions.text: Assertion (A): $7{,}344$ is divisible by $24$. Reason (R): $7{,}344$ is divisible by $3$ and by $8$, and $3$ and $8$ have no common factor. Choose: (i) both true, R explains A (ii) both true, R does not explain A (iii) A true, R false (iv) A false, R true.
questions.answer: (i). $344=8\times43$ and the digit sum is $18$. Since $3$ and $8$ are co-prime, the number is divisible by $24$: $7344=24\times306$.

questions.text: Assertion (A): The sum of four consecutive numbers is a multiple of $4$. Reason (R): The sum of four consecutive numbers is $4n+6$. Choose (i), (ii), (iii) or (iv) as above.
questions.answer: (iv). R is true, but $4n+6=4(n+1)+2$ leaves remainder $2$, so A is false.

sections.title: Section F · Digits in disguise
sections.note: Each letter stands for a digit. Different letters are different digits.

questions.text: $AB$ is a two-digit number with digits $A$ and $B$. $AB+BA=132$ and $A-B=2$. Find $AB$.
Solve $\begin{array}{r}1A\\\times\ \ A\\\hline 9A\end{array}$ ($A$ is a digit).
questions.answer: $A\times A$ ends in $A$: $A=0, 1, 5, 6$. $(10+A)A=90+A$ gives $A^2+9A-90=0$, so $A=6$. Check: $16\times6=96$.

questions.text: Find the digits: $\begin{array}{r}A\,B\\+\,B\,A\\\hline 1\,6\,5\end{array}$ with $A>B$. How many answers are there?
